correctness.rationale: A projective-plane incidence proof exhausts the zero-mono-line and one-mono-line cases after excluding two mono lines. Distinct-colour constraints use unique joining lines and intersections, with no algebraic or order-specific assumptions. A construction proves sharpness. Disjoint counting gives the falling factorial formula and spectrum; degree comparison uses the actual hypergraph incidence degree. A standalone checker enumerates all 877 Fano set partitions and all specified constructive prime-plane witnesses. Finite work corroborates rather than proves the unbounded theorem.

evidence: For line hypergraphs of projective planes distinct hyperedges meet in exactly one vertex, contrary to the overlap-at-least-two hypothesis in Piehowski Lemma 4.1.
Noncollinear triples exist for q≥2, so the r-complete hypothesis of Piehowski Cor. 4.0.1 fails.
Piehowski Lemma 4.4 gives the nonsharp upper bound \(\chi([H]_2)=q^2+q+1\); the Cor. 4.3.1 incidence-degree inequality is violated already by \(\operatorname{PG}(2,2)\), with \(5>3+1\).

originality.rationale: A new complete projective-plane line-hypergraph lean-colouring classification is not implied by the valid claims of the initiating full-text paper: projective-plane line intersections fail wide-path hypotheses and noncollinear triples fail r-completeness; the 2-section bound is nonsharp. Its printed hypergraph-degree corollary is instead contradicted. The closest full-text finite-plane colouring paper studies rainbow-free colourings, a non-equivalent admissibility rule. Searches of published-finding corpus and relevant literature found no dominating or equivalent exact spectrum; residual literature risk is explicitly retained.
residual_risks: An equivalent elementary classification may be contained in literature using a different name for rainbow-or-monochromatic line colourings, beyond the indexed searches.

The initiating manuscript might intend a corrected bound based on the degree of the two-section graph. The present result refutes only the printed hypergraph-incidence-degree interpretation, not that valid two-section bound.
Independent audit of the new proof is not performed.

value.rationale: Determines the complete new lean-colouring spectrum and exact named-palette enumerator for every finite projective plane, including non-Desarguesian planes. The exact two-level spectrum has q-1 forbidden intermediate numbers, and the same natural family gives infinitely many and unbounded-ratio counterexamples to a published incidence-degree bound. This is a motivated canonical-design classification rather than an arbitrary small calculation or routine substitution.
